title: fix(auth): route Sign in and runtime assets to paths that are served
body:
## What

1. Sign in (`src/App.vue`) now reloads the current URL instead of navigating to `/oauth2/start?rd=…`.
2. The six page-relative runtime asset references are now root-relative (`/assets/...`):
   - `ViewModeCompact.vue:83` and `useViewerInitialization.js:285`: `hsy_po.json`
   - `helsinki.js:70`: `hki_po_clipped.json`
   - `populationgrid.js:184`: `hsy_populationgrid.json`
   - `useViewerInitialization.js:261` and `:264`: the two credit images

   The Helsinki Region Infoshare credit had the image path as its `title` tooltip. That line is edited anyway, and the new sweep flags the string, so the title is now "Helsinki Region Infoshare".
3. `unifiedLoader.loadStandard` checks `content-type` before parsing on the json, geojson and default branches. A non-JSON body throws `UnexpectedContentTypeError`, which names the URL and the content type. `loadLayer` records that message as the layer error.

Closes #994
Refs #941

## Why Sign in reloads instead of being removed

Checked against infrastructure `origin/main`, `argocd/apps/templates/regions4climate/`:
- `r4c-cesium-viewer-security-policy.yaml` targets the whole `r4c-cesium-viewer` HTTPRoute, which serves both the legacy and next backends on `r4c.dataportal.fi`. It sets `redirectURL: …/oauth2/callback`, `logoutPath: /oauth2/sign_out` and `forwardAccessToken: true`. It has no path exclusions and no `denyRedirect`.
- So Envoy serves only `/oauth2/callback` and `/oauth2/sign_out`, and there is no `/oauth2/start`. nginx adds only `location = /oauth2/userinfo` (`nginx/default.conf.template`). Every other `/oauth2/*` path gets the SPA shell. There, `CesiumViewer.vue` skips viewer init (#819), so the old Sign in left the user on a page with no map.

How `userStore` resolves behind Envoy: `fetch('/oauth2/userinfo')` passes the gateway with the session cookie, Envoy forwards the Google access token, and nginx exchanges it at Google's userinfo endpoint for the email. The store still ends up anonymous in these cases:
- Google rejects the forwarded token, so the response is non-2xx.
- No token was forwarded. nginx answers 401, which is the local `vite preview` and dev case.
- The body is not JSON; the Vite SPA fallback in dev and preview produces this.
- The fetch throws. This is inferred from the Envoy config, not observed: if the session lapses between page load and the fetch, Envoy redirects the fetch to Google and the cross-origin redirect fails CORS.

Anonymous visitors cannot reach the app in production, but the anonymous state can still occur, and in dev it is the default. Removing the item would leave no recovery in that state. Because every path is gated, a full reload is the sign-in: it re-enters the OIDC flow when the session is gone and re-runs the userinfo fetch otherwise. In dev it is harmless. This is one line and needs no icon-map regeneration.

Not verified: that Envoy returns the user to the reloaded URL after the Google callback. The oauth2 filter docs do not say where the callback redirects.

## Why the loader guard leaves a missing header alone

The SPA catch-all always sends `text/html`. A missing header comes from some other upstream, and refusing it would drop data that parses fine; `datasource.loadGeoJsonDataSource` treats a missing header as non-JSON, but that path only loads same-origin static files. The real upstreams send JSON types: pygeoapi sends `application/json`, the Helsinki WFS sends `application/json;charset=UTF-8`, and the mock API sets `application/json`. The unit test pins both the `application/geo+json` pass and the missing-header pass.

## How it was verified

Tests written first:
- `tests/unit/services/runtimeUrls.test.js`, a static sweep over `src/`:
  - Every string-literal URL argument of `fetch(` and `loadGeoJsonDataSource(` is root-relative or absolute. It parses call arguments, so it finds `helsinki.js` and `populationgrid.js`, where the literal is on the line after the call.
  - No string literal starts with `assets/` or `./assets/`.
  - Every `/oauth2/*` literal is one of callback, sign_out or userinfo.
  - A control test requires the parser to see `/oauth2/userinfo` in `userStore.ts`.
- `tests/unit/services/unifiedLoaderContentType.test.js`: 8 tests covering the guard.
- `tests/e2e/nested-path-assets.spec.ts`: opens the app at `/a/b`, waits for the `PostCodes` data source to have entities, and asserts that every `/assets/data/` request went to the root and that no `pageerror` fired. It needs no database.

RED on the unfixed tree:
- The sweep reported 4 page-relative call arguments, 7 `assets/` literals (the six references plus the credit title) and `src/App.vue:241 /oauth2/start`.
- The three html cases in the guard test failed with `SyntaxError`.
- The E2E timed out after 60 s waiting for `PostCodes`. At the HTTP level, preview answered `/a/assets/data/hsy_po.json` with 200 `text/html` and `/assets/data/hsy_po.json` with `application/json`.

GREEN: all unit tests passed, and the E2E passed 3 of 3 with `--repeat-each=3`. The E2E ran against a `VITE_E2E_TEST=true` build under `vite preview --port 4290 --strictPort`, through a scratch Playwright config that only changes `baseURL`. Port 4173 was held by another process on the machine.

Mutation checks (fixed files snapshotted and restored from the snapshot):
- `helsinki.js` back to `./assets/…`: 2 sweep tests failed, naming `helsinki.js:68` and `:70`.
- Sign in back to `/oauth2/start`: the oauth2 sweep failed.
- Guard removed: 3 failed.
- Guard made strict on a missing header: the missing-header test failed.
- The E2E RED run above used the unfixed asset files.

Gates, run in the worktree:
- `bun run lint` passed.
- `bun run typecheck` exited 0.
- `bun run test:unit` passed: 57 files, 957 tests passed, 4 skipped.
- `bun run test:integration` passed: 2 files, 46 tests.
- `bun run build` exited 0.

Review follow-up (b03d825): the guard moved above the comment that describes the body-read timing span, which it had been inserted beneath; no behaviour change. Lint, typecheck, unit (957 passed, 4 skipped), integration (46 passed) and build were re-run after it, and the guard-removed mutation still fails 3 tests.

Not verified: behaviour behind the real Envoy gateway, because there is no staging host for it.

## Out of scope

- Other `response.json()` sites without a content-type guard, listed in #941's triage (for example `progressiveLoader.js`), are unchanged. #994 scopes the guard to `loadStandard`.

## Sibling PRs

This branch touches `App.vue`, `useViewerInitialization.js` and `helsinki.js`, which #1001, #993 and #1010 also edit. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against each of those branches exits 0 with no conflicts.

title: perf(preload): remove background preloads that nothing reads
body:
## What

This removes the three critical preloads from `backgroundPreloader.startCriticalPreload()`:

- `postal-codes-helsinki`, which fetched `/paavo`
- `heat-exposure-sample`, which fetched `/pygeoapi/collections/heatexposure_optimized/items?f=json&limit=100`, untrimmed
- `hsy-layer-info`, which fetched `/hsy-action?action_route=GetHierarchicalMapLayerGroups`

The NDVI preload stays. A new test, `tests/unit/services/backgroundPreloader.test.js`, keeps an unread preload or an unbounded pygeoapi `/items` URL from coming back.

Closes #972

## Why

No module reads those three cache keys. Every consumer fetches the same data itself: `socioEconomicsStore` fetches `/paavo`, `heatExposureStore` uses the trimmed `urlStore.heatExposure()` URL, and `BackgroundMapBrowser` fetches `/hsy-action`. Each preload was therefore a duplicate download during startup. The triage measured 796 KB for `/paavo`, 1,354,144 B for the heat sample and 317 KB for `/hsy-action`. The heat sample is the only `heatexposure_optimized` request in `src` that can exceed Sentry's 300 KB Large HTTP Payload threshold, which makes it the likely source of CESIUM-VIEWER-25. This is the same class of bug as #755: a fetch whose response nothing uses. Lauri accepted deleting all three in one PR.

The NDVI preload stays because its URL comes from `urlStore.ndviTiffUrl()`, the same getter `tiffImagery.js` uses, so the preload and the NDVI layer request the same URL.

The other half of #972 is on the server: pygeoapi serves `hsy_buildings_optimized` pretty-printed and uncompressed. That is tracked in ForumViriumHelsinki/infrastructure#2421. The 30 s full-body health polling in `DataSourceStatusBadge` is tracked in #997.

## How

`startCriticalPreload()` now queues only the NDVI dates, and a comment records why the other three were removed. The new test has two parts:

- (a) It calls `startCriticalPreload()` with the queue processor stubbed. Every queued item must either have its cache key appear in another `src` file (block and line comments are stripped first) or have its URL built by the consumer's own builder. The second route currently covers only NDVI, and the test checks it against `urlStore.ndviTiffUrl(date)`. Two controls keep the check from passing vacuously: the queue must not be empty, and the search must find `ndviTiffUrl(` in consumer code.
- (b) It sweeps every `/items` URL literal in `src` and requires a narrowing parameter: `bbox`, `postinumero`, `posno`, `grid_id`, `from_id`, `vtj_prt`, `koodi`, `limit=1` or `skipGeometry=true`. A control checks that the sweep sees at least 10 of urlStore's template-literal builders. Two dead paths are allowlisted by exact literal, with a reason for each, as follow-ups. `urlStore.collectionUrl` has no mounted consumer and is removed with `espooSurvey.js` in the dead-analysis-removal PR for #980; the entry can go once that lands. `backgroundPreloader.getLayerUrl` (four base URLs) serves only `preloadPostalCodeData`, which has no callers, and its `filter=postalCode=` is not a pygeoapi parameter.

## Verification

- RED before the fix: (a) reported `postal-codes-helsinki`, `heat-exposure-sample` and `hsy-layer-info`, and (b) reported `backgroundPreloader.js` with the `limit=100` heat URL.
- GREEN after the fix: 3 of 3 tests pass.
- Mutation checks, each restored from a file snapshot. Re-adding the heat-sample entry turned both (a) and (b) red. Appending `?preload=1` to the NDVI preload URL turned (a) red for all four NDVI dates, so the same-builder check has teeth. Renaming `bbox=` in `urlStore.hsyGridBuildings` turned (b) red, so the sweep reads template literals.
- Startup network capture with `bun run dev` and a Playwright script: one headless page, idle for 60 s. On origin/main the preloader requested `/paavo` at 6.8 s, the heat sample at 13.8 s and `/hsy-action` at 22.3 s, and the totals were `/paavo` 4, `/hsy-action` 4 and heat `limit=100` 1. With this change the preloader went straight to NDVI at 7.7 s, and the totals were `/paavo` 3, `/hsy-action` 3 and heat `limit=100` 0. The remaining requests come from the consumers and from `DataSourceStatusBadge`'s 30 s health poll (#997).
- Gates: `bun run lint` exit 0, `bun run typecheck` exit 0, `bun run test:unit` 56 files and 948 tests passed (4 skipped). Pre-commit hooks passed.

## Not verified

- `bun run test:integration` and `bun run build` were not run. No import, dependency or build config changed, and no integration test covers the preloader.
- The Sentry side needs Sentry access, which was not available: reading `http.response_content_length` on trace f062fe18433d4bc099b149e02dc42b2a, and confirming that CESIUM-VIEWER-25 stops after release. The link from that issue to this preload is inferred from sizes and code paths.
- The capture ran against the dev proxy, not production nginx.

## Sibling PRs in this run

The dead-analysis-removal PR deletes `urlStore.collectionUrl`. After both merge, the matching `ITEMS_ALLOWLIST` entry in this test matches nothing. It is harmless, because allowlist entries are matched by exact literal and an unused entry does not fail, and it can be removed then. No other PR in this run touches `backgroundPreloader.js`.

Follow-up issues filed in this round: #1028, #1032, #1035.

title: fix(flood): remove the previous flood layer when switching scenarios
body:
## What

`createFloodImageryLayer()` (`src/services/floodwms.js`) now pushes the flood `ImageryLayer` into `backgroundMapStore.floodLayers` through `markRaw`. `removeFloodLayers()` then finds and removes it, so switching scenarios in the background map browser replaces the previous flood layer instead of stacking on it, and "none" clears the map. The `backgroundMapStore` layer setters and `propsStore.setHSYWMSLayers` mark their layers raw as well.

## Why

Pinia returns array elements from state as reactive proxies. `ImageryLayerCollection.contains()` and `remove()` match by identity (`this._layers.indexOf(layer)`), so `removeFloodLayers()` never found the tracked layer. It then cleared the store array, and the layer stayed on the map with nothing tracking it. `BackgroundMapBrowser.vue` calls `removeFloodLayers()` before adding a scenario and in `clearSelection()`, so every scenario switch added a layer. `tests/unit/services/floodwms.test.js` could not see this: it mocks the stores as plain objects and `contains` as always `true`. #1016 fixes the same bug for the land-cover layer.

## How

- `floodwms.js`: `backgroundMapStore.floodLayers.push(markRaw(addedLayer))`, the pattern `globalStore.setCesiumViewer()` uses for the viewer and #1016 uses for land cover.

title: fix(control-panel): keep the sidebar inert until the Cesium viewer is ready
body:
## What

The sidebar's tab content is now inert until the Cesium viewer exists, with a small "Loading map…" status hint above it. Tabs and the rail toggle stay usable. If viewer initialisation fails, the hint is replaced by "The map failed to load." and a Reload button, and the tab content stays inert. The 22 `void <call>(` sites in `src/` now handle their promise instead of discarding it.

Closes #951

## Why

`ControlPanel` mounts in the same tick as `CesiumViewer`, but its controls call `getCesium()` and read `globalStore.cesiumViewer`. Both exist only after the lazy Cesium chunk has loaded and the viewer is built. A click in that window either threw "Cesium accessed before initialization" (Sentry REGIONS4CLIMATE-3Y: Background Maps, a `v-list-item` click into `selectBasicMap`) or dereferenced a null viewer. Some handlers change UI state before they throw, so Satellite showed as selected with no layer behind it.

Where the call went through `void someAsync()`, the throw became an unhandled rejection with no context. The Land Cover switch and the HSY year select both reached `getCesium()` that way, through `void createHSYImageryLayer()`.

## How

- `ControlPanel.vue` gates `.sidebar-content` on `globalStore.cesiumViewer` with `inert`. A non-null viewer implies the module is loaded, so one gate closes both the not-loaded and the null-viewer windows, and the ~85 `getCesium()` call sites stay as they are. This follows "Gate UI on initialized for Async-Fetched State" in `.claude/rules/code-quality.md`.
- When initialisation fails, the viewer is never set, so the gate needs an end state besides "ready". `useViewerInitialization` sets the new `globalStore.viewerInitFailed` on both failure paths: a Cesium chunk that does not load (caught, error snackbar shown) and a `Cesium.Viewer` constructor that throws (for example without WebGL; logged, flag set, then rethrown as before, with CesiumWidget's own error panel over the map and no snackbar). `ControlPanel` then shows a `role="alert"` notice (`.viewer-init-error`) with a Reload button that calls `window.location.reload()`, in place of the loading hint. `retryInit` clears the flag, so a retry shows the loading hint again and a successful retry opens the gate.
- Each `void <call>(` site now ends in `.catch((error) => logger.error(…))`. `UnifiedSearch.selectAddress` is synchronous, so its `void` is simply removed. The two `void nextTick(cb)` sites are included, because a throw in the callback rejects `nextTick`'s promise in the same way.
- `cesiumTest`'s CI path does not wait for the real viewer, so it now waits for the hint to detach before it hands over the page. While the gate is closed, `click()` retries until it times out and `fill()` silently types nothing (checked with a probe spec against the gated build). The hint also detaches when initialisation fails, so the fixture then logs `Viewer initialisation failed (.viewer-init-error shown)` before it continues (commit `00cd82f`); without that line the case left no trace in the test output.
- `.claude/rules/testing.md` documents the gate for spec authors. `.claude/rules/code-quality.md` names the test that enforces the no-`void` rule.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/pages/ControlPanel.preinit.test.js` mounts the panel with the real, uninitialised `cesiumProvider` and a null viewer. It clicks every button, list item, tab, switch and field, round after round, runs a search, and asserts that no Vue error, unhandled rejection or logged pre-init error occurs. It names no handler. jsdom has no `inert`, so the test skips elements under `[inert]`, the way a browser would.
- `tests/e2e/sidebar-before-viewer.spec.ts` holds the Cesium chunk with `page.route`. It clicks Satellite, the Land Cover switch and the search field with `page.mouse`, then releases the chunk and checks that the same controls work. The checks made while the chunk is held are hard assertions, because this PR fixes the contract they pin (`.claude/rules/testing.md` reserves `expect.soft()` for known-broken contracts). It is skipped on the Mobile Chrome project, where the LoadingIndicator banner covers the drawer after init.
- `tests/unit/lint/no-void-calls.test.js` fails on any new `void <call>(` in `src/`. A control case checks that the pattern still matches the forms it bans.
- `tests/unit/pages/ControlPanel.initFailure.test.js` mounts the panel, then runs the real `useViewerInitialization` with its init made to fail. Only the Cesium module (spies on the real provider) and the service-module loader are replaced. It covers a rejected Cesium chunk and a throwing `Viewer` constructor. For each, it asserts that the loading hint is gone, an alert reads "map failed to load", the Reload button is outside any `[inert]` subtree, and the tab content is still inert. It also checks that Reload calls `location.reload()`, and that a retry which builds the viewer clears the flag and opens the gate.

## Verification

- `bun run lint`: exit 0. `bun run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `bun run test:unit`: 57 files, 950 passed, 4 skipped. `bun run test:integration`: 2 files, 46 passed.
- `bun run build` and `VITE_E2E_TEST=true bun run build`: both exit 0.
- RED against `origin/main`'s source: the void test listed the 22 sites. The sweep reported 19 Vue errors (Default Map, Satellite, Terrain, Parks, Climate Adaptation, Go back and others), 4 unhandled rejections and 1 logged pre-init error. The inert test failed.
- Mutation, gate removed with the `.catch` fixes kept: the sweep went red on Vue errors and logged pre-init errors, and the rejection channel was empty. Restored from a snapshot.
- Mutation, `void createHSYImageryLayer()` put back in `HSYYearSelect.vue`: the void test went red and named `HSYYearSelect.vue:33`. Restored from a snapshot.
- E2E, run against a `VITE_E2E_TEST=true` build under `vite preview` on a private port (the build CI uses): 8 of 8 passed on chromium. With the gate removed and the app rebuilt, it failed 2 of 2 with all five symptoms: no `inert`, search text accepted, Land Cover checked, Satellite marked selected, and "Cesium accessed before initialization" logged. That run used the earlier soft assertions.
- Review re-run, after the hold-window checks became hard assertions (commit `4230cbf`): lint, typecheck, `test:unit` (57 files, 950 passed, 4 skipped), `test:integration` (46 passed) and `bun run build` all exit 0. The E2E spec passed 3 of 3 on chromium against a `VITE_E2E_TEST=true` build under `vite preview` on a private port. With the `:inert` binding removed and the app rebuilt, it failed at the first hold-window check (the `inert` attribute). The unit sweep went red on the same mutation (19 Vue errors, and the inert test failed). Against `origin/main`'s `src/`, the void test listed the same 22 sites.
- `tests/e2e/basic.spec.ts` via `cesiumTest`, both with `CI=true` (the fixture's CI path) and without: 3 passed, 1 failed ("Statistical Grid View"). That test fails the same way on an `origin/main` build.
- Init-failure fix (commit `88b7019`), RED first: against `4230cbf` the new test failed 4 of 4, each at the assertion that the loading hint is gone. After both failure paths, "Loading map…" was still rendered and `cesiumViewer` was null.
- Mutations, each restored from a snapshot: flag removed from the chunk path turned the chunk test red (1 of 4). Flag removed from the constructor path turned the constructor, Reload and retry tests red (3 of 4). The flag reset removed from `retryInit` turned the retry test red at the `viewerInitFailed` assertion (1 of 4). A no-op `reloadPage` turned the Reload test red (1 of 4). Leaving the content non-inert on failure turned the chunk, constructor and retry tests red at the inert assertion (3 of 4).
- After the fix: `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` exit 0. `bun run test:unit`: 58 files, 954 passed, 4 skipped. `bun run build` exit 0.
- Browser, `vite preview` of that build on a private port, with the `cesiumSymbols` chunk aborted by `page.route`: the chunk was requested twice (the preload handler's automatic reload, then its reload guard held). The sidebar then showed "The map failed to load. Reload" with `role="alert"`, no loading hint, and inert tab content. Clicking Reload navigated. The control run without interception showed neither element and non-inert content.
- Review round on `88b7019`, then `00cd82f`: lint and typecheck exit 0, `test:unit` 58 files with 954 passed and 4 skipped, `test:integration` 46 passed, `bun run build` exit 0. Against `4230cbf`'s three `src` files with the new test kept, the test failed 4 of 4. A `role="status"` notice in place of `role="alert"` turned 3 of 4 red.
- Review round, browser, a plain `bun run build` (the CI build) under `vite preview` on a private port. `sidebar-before-viewer.spec.ts` passed. With the `cesiumSymbols` chunk aborted, the chunk was requested twice and the page navigated twice, then `.viewer-init-error` was visible with `role="alert"`, the hint was gone, the content was inert and the Reload button took keyboard focus. The error snackbar's alert was present as well. ## Not verified

- The E2E spec was not run against the dev server (`just test-e2e`). The route pattern matches `/src/services/cesiumSymbols.js` by construction only.
- Against a plain build (no `VITE_E2E_TEST`), the spec once timed out waiting for the Layers panel to stop moving (`scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`, "waiting for element to be stable"). It passed on a plain build in the review round, so that timeout is intermittent (#1023); it was not investigated.
- The full E2E and accessibility suites were not run. They need a database, and those CI jobs are already red on `main` (#947).

title: feat(vtt-flood): add synthetic data flag for demos when the VTT API is down
body:
## What

Adds a `vttFloodSyntheticData` developer feature flag. When it is on, the VTT flood simulation panel renders locally generated frames instead of calling `/vtt-api`.

## Why

The VTT API returned `504` for `scenario=1 frame=0`, so the panel showed only an error and the feature could not be demoed.

## How

- `src/services/vttFloodSynthetic.js` builds a deterministic 24×18 grid of ~100 m cells around Laajasalo, in the same GeoJSON shape the API returns, with all four dimensions. Rain follows a per-scenario profile (80 mm over 1 h for scenario 1; 30 mm and 40 mm over 12 h for scenarios 2 and 3), collects in three fixed depressions, and drains after the storm. The values are illustrative, not a hydrological model.
- `fetchSimulationFrame` takes a `synthetic` option. The store passes the flag value, so validation, range computation and rendering run unchanged.
- The panel shows a **Synthetic data** chip and reloads the current frame when the flag is toggled while the panel is open.
- The flag is registered in `flagMetadata.ts`, `flags.goff.yaml` (default disabled) and `docs/core/FEATURE_FLAGS.md`.

## Enabling for a demo

Turn on `VTT Flood Synthetic Data` in the Feature Flags panel, or run:

```js
localStorage.setItem('featureFlags', JSON.stringify({ vttFloodSimulation: true, vttFloodSyntheticData: true }))
```

## Verification

- `bunx vitest run` on `vttFlood`, `vttFloodSynthetic` and `featureFlagStore` tests: 96 passed
- `bun run typecheck`: no errors
- `bun run lint`: clean
- Not checked by eye in the running app.

title: test(cesium): guard the cesiumSymbols export list against drift
body:
## What

This adds `tests/unit/services/cesiumSymbols.test.js`, a static check that `src/services/cesiumSymbols.js` exports every Cesium symbol the app reads. It covers the gap #959 named: code that reaches the module through the untyped `window.__cesium` handle. The module's JSDoc now points at the test. It is the closing PR for #817.

Closes #817

## Why, and the state of #817's three items

- **Item 2 (tree-shaking)** landed in #959 (28c1c2c). `cesiumProvider.initialize()` imports the 38 named re-exports in `cesiumSymbols.js` instead of the `cesium` namespace. That PR measured the lazy Cesium graph going from 4,734,447 B to 4,074,082 B raw (−13.95%) and from 1,289,709 B to 1,082,090 B gzip (−16.10%). Since then, a symbol missing from the list is `undefined` at runtime. `vue-tsc` reports the omission at `getCesium()` call sites, but not for code that reads the module through `window.__cesium`. The E2E fixture reads `ShadowMode` that way, and dropping it would fail only when that spec ran. This test closes that gap.
- **Item 1 (route-gate the Cesium load)**: Lauri accepted dropping it. The map is the app's only view, so there is no route to gate. The app has no router, and `App.vue` mounts `<CesiumViewer />` unconditionally. Gating on a gesture would put the Cesium download behind a click and lengthen the pre-init window tracked in #951.
- **Item 3 (re-measure)**: Lauri accepted Lighthouse CI on `main` as the measurement. There is no preview deploy. Lighthouse CI logged LCP between 1.97 s and 2.23 s in runs from 2026-06-30 to 2026-09-16. The pre-#814 run logs have expired, so no before/after pair can be produced.

## How the test works

It reproduces the list's regenerate command statically:

- **What it collects:** every member read off a Cesium module reference in `src/`, and in the test code that runs in a browser against the real module. That test code is everything under `tests/` except `tests/unit`, `tests/integration`, `tests/mocks` and `tests/setup.js`, which run against mocks.
- **Module references:** `Cesium`, any local bound to `getCesium()`, `cesiumProvider.get()`, `cesiumProvider.initialize()` or `window.__cesium`, and direct `__cesium.X` or `getCesium().X` reads.
- **Ignored:** comments, because JSDoc `Cesium.X` names are types that resolve through `src/types/cesium-global.d.ts`, not runtime reads. `window.Cesium.X` is also skipped, because the app never sets `window.Cesium`; only the CI mock fixture does.
- **Assertions:** every collected name is in the export block. A second assertion fails on destructuring (`const { X } = getCesium()`, or `const { X } = Cesium` from any local alias) or computed access (`Cesium[...]`), because the sweep cannot see those reads. Controls check that the export parse finds at least 30 names including `Viewer`, and that the sweep finds `Cartesian3` in `src` and `Math` and `ShadowMode` through the `__cesium` aliases in `tests/`.

## Verification

- At HEAD the guard passes (3 of 3). There is no drift, which matches the triage sweep. It collects 33 names from `src` and 6 from browser-run tests, through the aliases `Cesium`, `CesiumLib` and `CesiumRef`.
- Mutation checks, each restored from a file snapshot:
  - `ShadowMode` removed from the export list: red, reporting `ShadowMode (tests/fixtures/cesium-fixture.ts)`. This is the case `vue-tsc` cannot catch.
  - `Cartesian3` removed: red, listing each `src` reader (CoolingCenter.vue, camera.js, ControlPanel.vue and others).
  - `const { SceneMode } = getCesium()` added to `camera.js`: the untracked-access assertion went red with `destructured Cesium module`.
  - `Cesium.Math` changed to `Cesium.CesiumMath` in `camera-controls.spec.ts`: red, reporting `CesiumMath (tests/e2e/accessibility/camera-controls.spec.ts)`.
  - Review follow-up: `const { NotARealCesiumExport } = Cesium` added to `tests/e2e/helpers/cesium-helper.ts` kept all three tests green on the first commit, because only destructuring straight off `getCesium()` or `__cesium` was detected. The second commit also flags destructuring from a local alias; the same mutation now fails with `destructured Cesium module via Cesium`, and so does `const { Foo } = CesiumRef` in `tests/fixtures/cesium-fixture.ts`. `const { toRadians } = Cesium.Math` stays green, because `Cesium.Math` is already counted as a read.
- Gates: `bun run lint` exit 0, `bun run typecheck` exit 0, `bun run test:unit` 56 files and 948 tests passed (4 skipped). Pre-commit hooks passed. `bun run build` was not run, because the only source change is a JSDoc comment.

## Scope notes

- This is a subset check (every read name must be exported), so removing a usage never fails it. The dead-analysis-removal PR for #979, #980 and #981 is #1013. This branch starts from `main`, not stacked on it, and #1013 adds no Cesium reads: its one added `Cesium.` match is a `//` comment in `src/types/cesium-global.d.ts`, and the sweep skips `.d.ts` files. Once that PR lands, the export list can be regenerated to drop symbols it no longer uses. The diffs of the open sibling PRs #993, #999, #1000, #1001, #1003, #1004, #1006, #1008, #1011, #1012 and #1014 add no `Cesium.` reads. #1010 adds `Cesium.Color.ORANGE`, and `Color` is exported.
- Follow-up, not changed here: the module JSDoc says `FeatureDetection` is reached through `window.__cesium`. The only test read of it is `window.Cesium.FeatureDetection` in `tests/e2e/helpers/cesium-helper.ts`, and `window.Cesium` is the CI mock. So no code reads `FeatureDetection` from the real module today, and the export may be unneeded. `DataSource`, `ImageryLayerCollection`, `PropertyBag` and `TileProviderError` appear in `src` only in JSDoc types. Pruning the list is a bundle-size question for a separate change.

title: perf(deckgl): request 512 px WMS tiles to match the Cesium path
body:
## What

The deck.gl grid view now requests its HSY WMS underlay in 512 px tiles, which matches every Cesium `WebMapServiceImageryProvider`. `src/utils/deckglWms.js` exports `WMS_TILE_SIZE = 512`, and `buildWmsGetMapUrl()` uses it as the default. `DeckGlGridView.vue` passes the same constant to both the `TileLayer` `tileSize` and the GetMap call. A new static test, `tests/unit/utils/wmsTileSizeParity.test.js`, keeps all these sites at the same size. `.claude/rules/architecture.md` gains a tile-size parity bullet next to the shared-palette invariant.

Closes #966

## Why

deck chooses tile zoom as `round(zoom + log2(512 / tileSize))`, so a 256 px `TileLayer` loads one zoom level deeper and requests about four times as many `/wms/proxy` GetMap tiles as 512 for the same view. title: fix(sentry): drop GOFF background-reconnect rejections in beforeSend
body:
## What

`Sentry.init` in `src/main.js` gets `beforeSend: dropGoffRejectionEvent`. The new hook in `src/services/featureFlagProvider.ts` applies the existing `isGoffRejection` classifier to `hint.originalException` and drops matching events. All three rejection shapes the classifier knows are covered: the websocket-init timeout (#735, R4C-CESIUM-VIEWER-1Z), the GoFeatureFlag URL `TypeError` (#738) and the plain `{response, responseHeaders, statusCode}` object (#794, R4C-CESIUM-VIEWER-21).

The GOFF `unhandledrejection` listener keeps `event.preventDefault()`, which silences the browser's "Uncaught (in promise)" console line. Its JSDoc no longer claims that it keeps the events out of Sentry. `installGoffRejectionHandler` is now exported so the test can install the real listener.

Closes #956

## Why

Sentry's globalHandlers integration captures rejections by assigning `window.onunhandledrejection` during `Sentry.init`. In the installed `@sentry/browser`/`@sentry/core` 10.54.0, that handler calls `captureEvent` unconditionally. Neither package references `defaultPrevented` (0 hits; the control term `onunhandledrejection` has 4 and 3 hits). So the `preventDefault()` from #735 only affected the console, and every GOFF rejection kept reaching Sentry.

`beforeSend` was chosen over an `ignoreErrors` pattern because shape C has no message of its own. Sentry reports it as "Object captured as promise rejection with keys: response, responseHeaders, statusCode". A Cesium `RequestErrorEvent` produces exactly the same text, as the test run below shows. Only the classifier's plain-object check tells the two apart, and that check needs the original value.

## How it was verified

Test written first: `tests/unit/services/goffSentryFilter.test.ts`, 11 tests in three parts.

1. The filter on its own. It drops each GOFF shape (websocket string, websocket Error, GoFeatureFlag TypeError, plain three-key object, null-prototype object). It keeps an unrelated Error, a Cesium `RequestErrorEvent`, and an event with no original exception.
2. A real `BrowserClient` with `globalHandlersIntegration` and a spy transport. Sentry is initialised first and the real GOFF listener second, the same order as production. Each shape is dispatched as a `PromiseRejectionEvent`. The test asserts that the listener cancelled every GOFF event and that only the two controls reached the transport. Vitest's jsdom global does not forward Sentry's `onunhandledrejection` assignment to jsdom's event-handler attribute. The test therefore registers that handler as a listener in the position a browser would give the attribute; this is commented in the test.
3. A static sweep. Every global `unhandledrejection`/`error` listener in `src/` that calls `preventDefault()` must be allowlisted with a filter, and `src/main.js` must wire that filter as `beforeSend`. The only such listener is `featureFlagProvider.ts`.

RED on the unfixed code (`src/main.js` and `featureFlagProvider.ts` at `origin/main`): 10 of 11 tests failed; part 2 fails in setup there because the helpers are not exported yet. With the exports present and the filter made to return the event unchanged, part 2 received 7 events instead of 2, and all five GOFF shapes leaked with `defaultPrevented === true`, which reproduces #956 through the real listener.

Mutation checks (fixed files snapshotted and restored from the snapshot):
- `dropGoffRejectionEvent` returns the event unchanged: 6 failed (the five drop cases and the real-client test).
- `beforeSend` removed from `src/main.js`: 1 failed (the static wiring test).
- `event.preventDefault()` removed from the listener: 2 failed (the real-client `defaultPrevented` assertion and the sweep).

Gates, run in the worktree:
- `bun run lint` passed (174 files, no fixes).
- `bun run typecheck` exited 0.
- `bun run test:unit` passed: 56 files, 956 tests passed, 4 skipped.
- `bun run build` exited 0, with no new chunk warnings. `featureFlagProvider` was already statically imported by `App.vue` and `featureFlagStore.ts`.

Not verified: behaviour in production Sentry. The Sentry MCP was unauthenticated during triage. After release, resolve R4C-CESIUM-VIEWER-1Z and check -21, so that a recurrence opens a new group. E2E specs were not run; nothing here is visible in the UI.

## Sibling PRs

`src/main.js` is also edited by #1006, the Sentry environment-tagging PR for #995 (the `environment:` line and the `logger.debug` block; `git merge-tree` of the two branches is conflict-free) and by the dead-analysis-removal PR (the Pinia `stateTransformer`, around lines 91-96). The `beforeSend` line sits after `profilesSampleRate`, and the import goes in the second import block. None of the three edits overlap.

Follow-up issues filed in this round: #1029.

title: fix(ci): make Lighthouse CI survive hung Cesium loads
body:
## Problem

The `Lighthouse CI` workflow fails on `main` and every PR. `lhci collect` dies with:

```
"runtimeError": { "code": "PROTOCOL_TIMEOUT",
  "message": "Waiting for DevTools protocol response has exceeded the allotted time. (Method: Network.getResponseBody)" }
```

then `ERROR: No lhr-*.json files found in .lighthouseci/` → `Lighthouse CI failed: No Lighthouse report files found` (exit 1). The existing source-map workaround (#831, `LIGHTHOUSE=true` drops Cesium maps) is already merged at the failing HEAD — it is not the cause now.

## Root cause (run 26872355387)

A four-step chain:

1. `startServerReadyTimeout: 30000` expires before `bun run preview` prints a line matching `'Local:'` (the bun-script wrapper banner shadows vite's `➜  Local:` line) → lhci navigates against an unconfirmed server.
2. The page never reaches load (`Timed out waiting for page load. Checking if page is hung...`) — Cesium keeps fetching tiles, so the network never quiets and the 90s `maxWaitForLoad` ceiling is hit.
3. The incomplete trace crashes the **RootCauses** gatherer: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'frame_sequence')`, cascading to **TraceElements** and every LCP/layout/render-blocking audit. This is a Lighthouse **12.0/12.1** trace_engine bug — [GoogleChrome/lighthouse#16406](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/issues/16406), fixed by PR #16412 in a later 12.x. `@lhci/cli@0.14.x` bundles Lighthouse 12.0.0–12.1.0 (the broken range).
4. `Network.getResponseBody` PROTOCOL_TIMEOUT on the main document (SPA app-shell class — [GoogleChrome/lighthouse#10876](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/issues/10876)) makes lhci emit a `runtimeError` and **no `lhr-*.json`**.

## Fix (core only — no `skipAudits`)

The job only needs to **produce a report** (assertions are non-blocking `warn`). Two layered changes:

- **Pin `@lhci/cli@0.15.0`** (Lighthouse 12.6.1) so the `frame_sequence` trace_engine crash is gone (#16412). Replaces all three `@lhci/cli@0.14.x` calls in `lighthouse.yml`.
- **Harden server readiness**: call vite directly (`bunx vite preview --host --port 4173`), match `localhost:4173`, raise `startServerReadyTimeout` to 60s — so navigation doesn't start before the preview server is up.

Deliberately **not** skipping the six trace-element audits (`largest-contentful-paint-element`, `lcp-lazy-loaded`, `layout-shifts`, `non-composited-animations`, `prioritize-lcp-image`, `render-blocking-resources`) — pinning 0.15 should remove the crash class and keep those as real (non-blocking) signal. If CI still flakes on a Cesium hang, skipping them is the follow-up lever.

## Verification

This PR is its own verification vehicle — the `Lighthouse CI` workflow runs on PRs. Watch the check on this PR; success = an `lhr-*.json` is produced and the job is green.

```
LIGHTHOUSE=true bun run build && bunx @lhci/cli@0.15.0 collect --config=lighthouserc.cjs && ls -la .lighthouseci/lhr-*.json
```

Sources:
- https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/issues/16406 (frame_sequence / trace_engine, fixed #16412)
- https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/issues/10876 (Network.getResponseBody on main content, SPA app-shell)
